PullRequest.Title: Chat: Plugins opens Customizations > Plugins in every window
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #348690

In the regular VS Code window, **Chat: Plugins** (`workbench.action.chat.managePlugins`, also used by the `/plugins` slash command) opened the Extensions view filtered by `@agentPlugins`. That view only says "Find Agent Plugins in Customizations" with a **Browse Agent Plugins** button, so it costs an extra click. Only the Agents window opened Chat Customizations directly; #347469 added that because the Agents window has no Extensions view.

With this change, `ManagePluginsAction` opens Chat Customizations at the Plugins section in every window. The now unused `IWorkbenchEnvironmentService` and `IExtensionsWorkbenchService` imports are removed.

## How it was tested

- Scenario (validate-ui-scenario): run **Chat: Plugins** from the Command Palette and assert that `.ai-customization-management-editor` is visible with **Plugins** selected.
  - Installed Insiders 1.148.0-insider, Linux: **fails**. The sidebar shows "Extensions: Agent Plugins" and Customizations does not open.
  - Dev build of this branch (`--dev`), Linux: **passes**. Customizations opens with Plugins selected.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/chatPluginActions.ts`: passed.
- No unit test added: the action has no existing tests and only runs one command.

Note on the dev run: on this Linux runner, the dev build's workbench doesn't load with the `registerFileProtocol` `vscode-file://` handler (hundreds of module requests fail with `net::ERR_FAILED`). For the recording only, the compiled `out/` handler was temporarily switched to `protocol.handle` with `fs.readFile`. That patch is not part of this PR, and it touches nothing this change depends on.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat: Plugins from the Command Palette, or /plugins, in a regular window with local chat context; first open and subsequent opens.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits one OpenEditor command, which opens the singleton customization input and selects Plugins. Editor construction and section layout are synchronous; plugin refresh, sidebar counts, and migration recovery discovery are not awaited by the command. Local installed rows use the existing plugin-service snapshot. Previously the command opened the Extensions container; reaching Customizations required another navigation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover customization source folders and parse prompt-file metadata for sidebar/model data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared provider result per active source/cache generation, containing five prompt types; cold folder discovery and metadata reads scale with source folders and eligible files, not one full provider call per plugin row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This command did not itself open the customization editor in regular windows. These existing services could already be warm through other chat/customization consumers; the later Browse Agent Plugins navigation reached the editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sidebar/model population is asynchronous and is not awaited by ManagePluginsAction. In local context plugin rows can use the runtime-installed snapshot without waiting for all prompt counts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve GitHub references and read marketplace definition files when legacy marketplace browsing is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One snapshot request per widget generation, fanning out over M distinct marketplace references; warm successful GitHub results avoid requests. Empty/failing upstream results have different caching behavior, but the widget records a terminal snapshot state until reset.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: AgentPluginsListView.show already called fetchMarketplacePlugins for the unfiltered marketplace view. The new route keeps equivalent legacy discovery conditional and suppresses that snapshot when unified discovery is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background snapshot enrichment; editor opening does not await it. The old Extensions plugin view awaited its marketplace query before committing its list model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare or refresh Git marketplace repositories and read definition files; private GitHub discovery can fall back to this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Repository-level work over deduplicated marketplace references, not plugin entries. Warm valid repositories avoid cloning and skip refresh within the TTL; filesystem validity checks and definition reads can still occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old plugin marketplace query used the same repository preparation, per-key sequencer and TTL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of conditional background marketplace discovery; not awaited by the editor-opening command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check the recovery directory and load saved migration manifests; update orphaned running records when applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One root existence check when absent; otherwise one root listing and existence/read operations per recovery directory R. Status updates apply only to qualifying records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The regular-window command initially opened Extensions, not this editor. Recovery discovery already ran when the user subsequently opened Customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delayed background migration information refresh, not awaited by OpenEditor. Refreshes are coalesced and cancelled/superseded through the existing delayer/request lifecycle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed plugin count P, customization files F across five prompt types, source folders, and distinct configured marketplaces M after canonical-ID deduplication. Migration recovery records R contribute background reads.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One editor-opening command per user invocation. The input is singleton-style. Item-source cached promises coalesce section/count requests. Prompt metadata discovery uses a service-wide limiter of 10. Marketplace repositories run concurrently across distinct references but clone operations serialize per repository key. Recovery manifests are read sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing item-source promises are reused per session and harness descriptor until source-change invalidation. Prompt discovery has cached promises and per-type file-location caches when observed. Plugin marketplace snapshots distinguish uninitialized, loading, loaded and failed; they load only when visible and legacy browsing is enabled, and do not repeatedly retry failures. Successful GitHub marketplace results have an eight-hour persisted TTL; clone refresh uses the same age threshold.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in command and slash-command reachability, singleton input, asynchronous list/count paths, provider coalescing, marketplace grouping and shared discovery limiter, based on inspected implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or representative large-workspace profiles are available. Cold editor construction adds bounded UI work; file and recovery counts vary. The command change does not establish a new repeated invocation, cache invalidation loop, or boundary multiplication.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable high-confidence regression. The change directly opens the requested existing management surface rather than its intermediate Extensions destination. Its expected initialization work is bounded/coalesced, and marketplace fan-out is not newly multiplied.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat: Plugins in a regular window whose focused chat selects an agent-host harness, including Copilot CLI.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: OpenEditor resolves the existing focused-session target, opens the editor, and selects Plugins. Authoritative session plugin rows require the cached provider result; cold provider resolution waits for grouped runtime inventory and plugin-content expansion. Migration information and contributed Canvases initialization are background work, not awaited by the command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read runtime plugin installation inventory from the resolved agent connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory operation per distinct runtime provider K per shared provider fetch, rather than per plugin. Zero operations when customization metadata has no runtime providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The regular-window command initially showed the Extensions plugin surface. The existing customization editor/provider did this work when subsequently opened; the PR changes the initial destination, not grouping or provider fetch multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed for authoritative session plugin data; background relative to editor opening, but can delay populated session rows on a cold source.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve agent-host plugin subdirectories and read supported customization-file metadata through the filesystem provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four initial directory resolves per uncached plugin root Pc, plus synthetic-agent namespace resolves and eligible agent/skill/rule metadata reads Fc. Unchanged URI/nonce/label expansions reuse cached children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Regular-window initial Extensions navigation did not request this editor's session provider. The later customization navigation already expanded plugins identically. No new per-row provider call or loss of expansion caching is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold provider completion waits for expansion, so session-row population can wait; the command itself does not await plugin refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request migration target source folders, configured marketplace inventory, and delegated MCP migration candidates where enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Source-folder requests group by distinct target type per enabled file category; marketplace inventory is one list call only when configured candidates exist; MCP discovery is one delegated category computation. Not one request per migration candidate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This existing migration discovery ran on customization editor opening, which previously required a separate navigation in regular windows. The PR adds no category or per-candidate request loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delayed background migration dashboard information; not awaited by editor opening or Plugins selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List canvas definitions and agent extension inventory for eligible visible chat owners when Canvases is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A definition request and, where a frontend session resource exists, one extension-inventory request per eligible visible owner V, not per canvas or extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same enabled contributed widget initialized when users opened Customizations. The initial regular-window Plugins command now reaches that existing initialization, without changing owner grouping or refresh frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Contributed widget initialization is background and does not block OpenEditor completion. Hidden-section layout/render suppression and owner/request disposal are existing behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct runtime providers K, cold plugin roots Pc, supported metadata files Fc within those roots, migration categories/target types, and visible canvas owner contexts V. Inventory operations group by provider or visible owner, not individual plugins/canvases.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Item-source cached promises coalesce plugin counts and list refreshes. Runtime inventories use Promise.all over distinct providers. Cold plugin expansion runs across roots, with four initial directory resolves per root and parallel metadata reads within supported categories; warm expansions avoid those reads. Migration categories run concurrently, with source-folder requests serialized by distinct target type within each category. Canvas definitions and extension inventory run together per visible owner.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PureItemProviderItemSource caches the whole provider promise per session/descriptor and clears failures for retry. Plugin expansion caches children by URI, nonce and plugin label. Warm repeated openings reuse source data unless invalidated. Canvas stores track owner lifetimes and current requests; only visible chat owners contribute. No diff changes any of these keys or invalidation rules.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in focused-session resolution, provider-level promise coalescing, runtime-provider grouping, expansion keys, category/type grouping and visible-owner canvas initialization. No evidence establishes a diff-created retry loop or repeated full expansion on warm opens.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold remote filesystem and host request durations, eligible plugin files, and visible-owner counts are unmeasured. Upstream service costs can vary; observed grouping and caches prevent interpreting them as per-plugin full-inventory calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence actionable performance regression established. The route now presents the existing authoritative session customization surface; potentially expensive cold reads are real, but the diff neither defeats its caches nor increases the effective per-fetch cardinality. Reworking unchanged provider expansion or hidden contributed sections would be scope expansion without stronger regression evidence.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat: Plugins in the Agents window, and command registration during startup.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Agents-window invocation already awaited the same OpenEditor command with the same Plugins target before the PR. Startup only registers the action; registration does not run it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reach the existing customization editor and its conditional filesystem, host-inventory, migration, canvas and marketplace boundaries described in the preceding scenarios.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly the same single editor command and transitive grouping as before; zero such operations during action registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed isSessionsWindow branch executed the exact same command and Plugins argument, then returned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Identical Agents-window opening path before and after. No new startup boundary is added.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The same installed plugins, provider groups, customization files, marketplaces, recovery records and visible canvas owners as existing customization-editor use. Registration occurs once, not per item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged editor singleton, provider promise coalescing, prompt discovery limiter, marketplace repository sequencer and background refresh scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All service, provider and widget caches retain their previous keys, successful/failed states and invalidation/disposal behavior. Import removals introduce no new startup service reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the diff preserves the exact previous Agents-window command call and only removes the regular-window alternate route.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing editor/host costs are unmeasured, but their Agents-window behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance mechanism in Agents-window invocation or startup registration.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete one-file inventory and both diff hunks, against base 559eab763ec8cbba4eb10cd61df616cb43019f4b. Traced the action, /plugins caller, old Extensions query, editor lifecycle, provider/count caches, local and remote discovery, marketplace repository grouping, background migration and visible-owner canvas inventory. No findings qualify; no concrete regression fix with a justified introducing commit was established. Static review only; no timings were inferred. The performance guide document was requested but the tool returned a truncated preview; learned-regressions guidance was available in full.
